exactness.note: Every checkpoint of the first rep of every cell was restored by a separate process; later reps verify their final checkpoint only (resume_mode=final).

fixture.description: the R11/R12b training-goodput fixture by construction

label: Session vs per-save service inside the real training-goodput loop; synthetic seeded model/data, single CPU host, no GPU, no fleet claim. Cold and warm service are reported separately.
losses: At 4 steps between checkpoints the session's clean training-step p50 is 1.12x the per-save service (12.29 ms vs 10.94 ms). The save work is the same; it is spread over more training steps because the session stops stalling the loop, so more of it overlaps a step on this single host.

At 4 steps between checkpoints the session's first checkpoint is 1.00x the per-save first checkpoint (112.9 ms vs 112.4 ms) because it pays the helper start and the first writable handle open that later saves reuse. The cold sample is n=1 per run.
At 4 steps between checkpoints the session had to wait 0.0 ms for the previous save before starting the next one (a save completing slower than the checkpoint interval).

At 16 steps between checkpoints the session's first checkpoint is 1.08x the per-save first checkpoint (123.7 ms vs 114.6 ms) because it pays the helper start and the first writable handle open that later saves reuse. The cold sample is n=1 per run.

The session holds a writable store handle between checkpoints, so for up to session_idle_secs after a save no other process can open the store for writing. That is a trade-off, not a free win, and it is why the session is opt-in.

Warm-service samples also include store-growth cost (a later commit in the same store climbs the index chain). The non-session arm has the same confound, so the comparison is fair but neither arm is a fresh-store number.
The kill court always loses the steps after the last acked checkpoint; the measured loss is the median steps_lost per scenario, not zero.

method.backend_fsyncs: the store's own per-save durability barrier count from the FINISH_CHECKPOINT reply
method.cold: the first completed checkpoint of each run: for weft-session this includes the helper start, the store open and the first writable handle upgrade; for weft it is just the first save
method.completion_ms: submit to the save worker's completion callback
method.loop_wall_ms: before step 1 to after the last save completes
method.service_requests: helper protocol requests observed per save (per-save arm only; the session arm's helper counters are cumulative)
method.session_stats: 'saves' and 'services_started' come from CheckpointSession; the session's writable_handle_opens field is not incremented by the shipped adapter and is not reported here
method.warm: every later completed checkpoint in the same run

non_claims: Single CPU host inside the Docker python court; no GPU, no GPU-direct, no NCCL, no multi-rank claim.
Synthetic seeded data and a 0.4M-parameter model, not a public corpus or a production model.
No queueing policy: a save that is still running blocks the next checkpoint, and that wait is measured, not absorbed silently.
Kill tests are SIGKILL process faults against a local store, not physical media power loss or host-cache loss.
The store is single-writer (MW1); no multi-writer training claim.
One host, warm page cache after the first repetition; no fleet or energy claim.
wins: At 4 steps between checkpoints the reused session's warm completion p50 is 0.20x the per-save service (43.2 ms vs 216.4 ms), on identical steps and data.

At 4 steps between checkpoints the session's training-thread pause p50 is 0.18x the per-save service (0.71 ms vs 3.99 ms): the submit no longer builds a writer and opens the store on the training thread.
At 8 steps between checkpoints the reused session's warm completion p50 is 0.33x the per-save service (42.4 ms vs 129.7 ms), on identical steps and data.

At 8 steps between checkpoints the session's training-thread pause p50 is 0.19x the per-save service (0.71 ms vs 3.67 ms): the submit no longer builds a writer and opens the store on the training thread.
At 16 steps between checkpoints the reused session's warm completion p50 is 0.48x the per-save service (42.1 ms vs 87.4 ms), on identical steps and data.

At 16 steps between checkpoints the session's training-thread pause p50 is 0.21x the per-save service (0.73 ms vs 3.51 ms): the submit no longer builds a writer and opens the store on the training thread.
At 32 steps between checkpoints the reused session's warm completion p50 is 0.57x the per-save service (40.5 ms vs 71.4 ms), on identical steps and data.

At 32 steps between checkpoints the session's training-thread pause p50 is 0.22x the per-save service (0.78 ms vs 3.59 ms): the submit no longer builds a writer and opens the store on the training thread.

The reused writable handle is where the save time goes away: server-side publish p50 is 26.2/26.1/26.8/25.7 ms (session) vs 80.2/53.1/40.0/33.6 ms (per-save) at 4/8/16/32 steps between checkpoints. The per-save arm reopens the store and replays the commit chain on every save, and that cost grows with the number of commits already in the store.

Durability is not traded away: every save in both arms reports the same backend barrier and write counts (528 fsyncs and 265 writes p50 per save at this fixture), so the session changes when the handle is opened, not what is durable before the save is acknowledged.
